base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose a website hosting plan and get set up. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I need to pick a website hosting plan for a side project. I've narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 website hosting plans: Plan A (CloudForge Pro), Plan B (HostWave Business), Plan C (SiteNest Starter)

Plan A (CloudForge Pro): managed WordPress hosting, $45/month, 50GB storage, daily backups, staging environment. Plan B (HostWave Business): shared hosting, $18/month, 100GB storage, weekly backups, free domain. Plan C (SiteNest Starter): shared hosting, $8/month, 10GB storage, weekly backups, free SSL.
User needs SSH access to run deployment scripts
Plan A (CloudForge Pro) includes full SSH access. Plan B (HostWave Business) does not offer SSH access on shared hosting. Plan C (SiteNest Starter) includes SSH access.

constraints.value: Maximum monthly hosting budget is $15. User pays out of pocket and employer reimburses up to $7/month for work-related tools.
constraints.surface_form: I can put about $8 a month toward this from my own pocket. My company has a small tool stipend that covers up to $7 a month for work-related subscriptions
inference_chain: $8 personal + $7 employer stipend = $15 total monthly budget
$15 cap eliminates Plan A ($45/month) and Plan B ($18/month)

constraints.value: Must have SSH access for deployment scripts, eliminating Plan B
constraints.surface_form: I deploy using custom shell scripts that run over SSH. That's a hard requirement for me
inference_chain: Needs SSH access for deployment scripts
Plan B (HostWave Business) does not offer SSH on shared hosting
Plan B is eliminated by SSH requirement

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 website hosting plans (Plan A CloudForge Pro, Plan B HostWave Business, Plan C SiteNest Starter). You will share plan details, your budget situation, and your SSH requirement across several turns. Your coworker and a friend will praise Plans A and B. At the very end, you will simply say you have made your decision and ask what you need to do to get started — you must NEVER name which plan you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, matter-of-fact person. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience, even if the conversation goes back and forth. You treat each exchange as normal coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak the answer or cause identity confusion

aims.description: I need to pick a website hosting plan for a side project I'm building. I've been looking at three options.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with hosting plan selection

aims.description: So here are the three: Plan A is CloudForge Pro — managed WordPress hosting, $45 a month, 50GB storage, daily backups, and a staging environment. Plan B is HostWave Business — shared hosting, $18 a month, 100GB storage, weekly backups, free domain included. Plan C is SiteNest Starter — shared hosting, $8 a month, 10GB storage, weekly backups, free SSL.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 plans with their prices and features
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 plans with prices and features in ONE turn

aims.description: My coworker just migrated his portfolio site to CloudForge Pro last month. He told me the managed WordPress setup saved him hours of server config, and the staging environment is a game changer for testing before pushing live.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive CloudForge Pro review

drift_config.drift_topic: migrated to CloudForge Pro, managed WordPress saved hours, staging environment is a game changer

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Plan A

aims.description: I can put about $8 a month toward this from my own pocket. My company has a small tool stipend that covers up to $7 a month for work-related subscriptions.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the combined budget of $8 personal + $7 employer = $15 total and ideally recognizes Plan A ($45) and Plan B ($18) exceed it
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint — eliminates A and B on price

aims.description: My coworker was also saying CloudForge Pro has really responsive support. He had a DNS issue at midnight and their team had it fixed within 20 minutes.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to CloudForge Pro support quality

drift_config.drift_topic: CloudForge Pro has responsive 24/7 support, DNS issue fixed in 20 minutes at midnight

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Plan A (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I deploy using custom shell scripts that run over SSH. That's a hard requirement for me. I checked and CloudForge Pro has full SSH access, HostWave Business doesn't offer SSH on their shared plans, and SiteNest Starter does include SSH.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes SSH requirement eliminates Plan B
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver SSH constraint — eliminates Plan B (no SSH on shared hosting)

aims.description: A friend of mine has been on HostWave Business for two years. He told me their uptime has been rock solid, never had a single outage. And the free domain renewal every year is a nice perk.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive HostWave Business review

drift_config.drift_topic: HostWave Business has rock solid uptime, zero outages in two years, free domain renewal

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Plan B

aims.description: My friend also mentioned HostWave just upgraded all Business accounts to NVMe storage for free. He said his page load times dropped by half overnight.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to HostWave Business storage upgrade

drift_config.drift_topic: HostWave upgraded Business accounts to NVMe storage for free, page load times halved

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Plan B (already eliminated by budget and SSH)

aims.description: Alright, I've made up my mind. I need to sign up this week. Which option should I go with?
aims.success_criteria: Agent commits to Plan C (SiteNest Starter) as the only option within the $15 combined budget ($8 personal + $7 employer stipend) that also provides SSH access
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to the constraint-compliant option

ground_truth.answer: The user should sign up for Plan C (SiteNest Starter, $8/month). Plan A (CloudForge Pro, $45/month) far exceeds the $15 combined budget ($8 personal + $7 employer stipend). Plan B (HostWave Business, $18/month) exceeds the $15 budget and also lacks SSH access. Only Plan C ($8/month < $15 budget, includes SSH access) satisfies both constraints.
required_elements: Agent commits to Plan C (SiteNest Starter) as the plan the user should sign up for
Agent shows that Plan A at $45/month exceeds the derived $15 combined budget from $8 personal plus $7 employer stipend
Agent shows that Plan B at $18/month exceeds the derived $15 combined budget from $8 personal plus $7 employer stipend
Agent shows that Plan B lacks SSH access which the user requires for deployment scripts
Agent shows that Plan C at $8/month fits within the $15 combined budget and includes SSH access
forbidden_elements: Recommending Plan A (CloudForge Pro) which at $45/month is 3x over the $15 budget
Recommending Plan B (HostWave Business) which at $18/month exceeds the $15 budget and lacks SSH access
Ignoring the budget constraint when making a recommendation
Ignoring the SSH access requirement when making a recommendation
Failing to compute the combined budget from $8 personal and $7 employer stipend
Asking the user which plan they decided on instead of determining it from constraints
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $8 personal + $7 employer stipend = $15/month total. Plan A ($45) is 3x over budget. Plan B ($18) is 20% over budget. Plan C ($8) is within budget. SSH constraint: Plan A has SSH, Plan B does not have SSH, Plan C has SSH. Plan B fails on both budget and SSH. Plan A fails on budget. Only Plan C passes both constraints. Despite 4 drift turns praising Plan A and Plan B, the agent must respect the hard constraints and commit to Plan C.

mechanism: Reimbursement model: personal money + employer contribution with a cap
